applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict grounded on what a single verse (Matthew 1:16) does or does not settle, which is exactly what the rule governs.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: 'does not state a link or its contrary': the judge reads a single verse as underdetermined because it 'admits both' readings rather than stating either link decisively; the alternative reading was that an ambiguous single verse, since it states something but equivocally, could ground UNDERDETERMINED — but the rule bars any single-verse ground, for either side and in either direction.
why: The judge rests UNDERDETERMINED entirely on one verse's failure to state the link (its grammar 'admits both' readings), which the rule forbids as a ground.
